full_judgment:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the petitioners, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 20-04-2010 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 2009 should not be declared illegal, without lawful authority and is no legal effect and as to why the provision of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (herein after referred to as Ain) for payment of 10% of the decretal amount by the 3rd party is illegal unlawful, detrimental to the fundamental principle of the Constitution as well as fundamental right of the Constitution of Bangladesh as well as the same is bad in law. 

 2. Background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the petitioners in the instant writ petition challenges the provision of section 32 of the Ain on the ground that the same is illegal ultra vires and against the fundamental right as guaranteed under Constitution. It has been stated that respondent No. 2 Agrani Bank Ltd. Hatkhola Branch, Dhaka filed Title Suit No.60 of 1998 in the first Court of Artha Rin Adalat and Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against ten persons impleading them as defendants. The suit was decreed and put to execution in Execution Case No.56 of 1999 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka. Petitioners thereafter came to know on 8-11-2009 from the respondent No.2 bank that the bank is going to sell the property pursuant to Money Execution Case. Under the circumstances the petitioners as third party filed an application under section32(2) of the Ain read with Order XXI Rule 58(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with section 57 of the Ain praying for exemption of their property. By order dated 6.01.2010 the Adalat rejected the said application with a finding that the petitioners as per provision of section 32(2) of the Ain did not file the bond of 10% of the decretal amount. Thereafter the petitioner by depositing an amount of Taka 4,89,000 through pay order from Mutual Trust Bank dated 19-4-2010 equivalent to 10% of the decreetal amount communicated it to the said Executing Court by filing another application and prayed for reconsideration of the petitioner's prayer for recalling the order dated 06-01-2010 and to reinstate the said Miscellaneous case No.54 of 2009. By the impugned order dated 20-04-2010 the said application was also rejected on the ground that the petitioner against the order dated 06-1-2010 and 26-1-2010 moved this Division for substantial relief and also filed this application long after 3 months which is barred by limitation and accordingly rejected the application. It is at this stage the petitioner moved this Division and obtained this present Rule and stay. 

 3. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners at the time of pronouncement of the judgment by filing affidavit in reply submits that the Executing Court erred in law in not holding that section 32(2) of the Ain has not prescribed any limitation and if an application is rejected due to some technical reason, filing of subsequent application has no bar and for that reason the impugned order is liable to be set-aside. Next he submits that the application dated 20-04-2010 which was rejected on the same date was under section 32(2) and section 57 of the Ain praying for a review of the order of rejection of the Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 2009 of the petitioner's case as a third party and the Court below should have consider his prayer at least in terms of section 57 of the Ain. Next he submits that the provision of section 32(2) of the Ain is against the constitutional provision as it has curtailing effect of fundamental right as enshrined under the Constitution. 

 9. Since the petitioners have made application both under Section 32 and 57 of the Ain, the same in not maintainable on that count owing to facts and circumstances of the case. In Md. Mansur Rahman vs. Abdul Mannan Sarder 7 ADC 623 our Appellate Division explained the scope of section 57 of Ain which would have a bearing on the point.
